title: FizzBuzz
instructorPromptText: Write a C program that asks the user for a positive integer N, then loops from 1 to N. For multiples of 3 print 'Fizz', for multiples of 5 print 'Buzz', for multiples of both print 'FizzBuzz', and for other numbers print the number itself.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program loop from 1 up to and including N?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Verifies correct loop boundary conditions (using `<=` instead of `<`), preventing off-by-one errors.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program check the double divisor condition (3 and 5) first, before checking individual divisors?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Checking `n % 3 == 0` first will intercept multiples of 15, printing 'Fizz' instead of 'FizzBuzz'. Logical ordering is a core control structure skill.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program print each string or number on a new line (e.g. using `\n` in `printf`)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Output formatting ensures readable console streams and allows automation parsers to check correctness.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student checks single divisibility first, resulting in multiples of 15 printing 'Fizz' or 'Buzz' instead of 'FizzBuzz'.
Student writes loop condition `i < n` instead of `i <= n`, omitting the final number.
Student prints 'Fizz' (without newline) followed conditionally by 'Buzz' (without newline), then falling back to number if neither printed — a clever conditional assembly.
Student uses logical OR `||` instead of AND `&&` to check if a number is a multiple of both 3 and 5.
Student prints extra explanatory prompts (e.g. 'The number is: Fizz') violating the exact output spec.
